Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L04_GuidedPractice_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.02

Which list best shows required parts of a quality speech outline?

answer.text: A. Random facts, jokes, and unrelated notes.

feedback.text: This does not follow accepted speech format or quality expectations.

answer.text: B. Introduction, focus, main points, support, transitions, and conclusion.

feedback.text: Correct. These parts create a clear speech product format.

answer.text: C. A title only.

feedback.text: A title alone is incomplete for speech planning.

answer.text: D. A paragraph with no labels.

feedback.text: This makes the structure hard to follow.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L04_GuidedPractice_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.SPK.01

Which note best supports oral presentation?

answer.text: A. Talk about everything and stuff.

feedback.text: This is vague and does not help the speaker present clearly.

answer.text: B. Say all words from full script.

feedback.text: This may lead to reading instead of presenting.

answer.text: C. Random idea, maybe transition.

feedback.text: This is unclear and incomplete.

answer.text: D. Point 1: planner shows deadlines; evidence: assignments listed by date.

feedback.text: Correct. This note gives a clear cue for organized speaking.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L04_GuidedPractice_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.04

Which sentence uses standard English conventions?

answer.text: A. My speech explains why note cards help speakers.

feedback.text: Correct. The sentence uses capitalization, subject-verb agreement, and clear wording.

answer.text: B. my speech explain why note cards helps speakers.

feedback.text: This has capitalization and subject-verb agreement errors.

answer.text: C. My speech explain why note-card cues helps speakers.

feedback.text: This has subject-verb agreement errors.

answer.text: D. my speech explains why note cards support delivery.

feedback.text: This needs capitalization at the beginning before it follows standard English conventions.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L04_GuidedPractice_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.02

A speech outline has an introduction, three points, and support, but no conclusion. What is the best revision?

answer.text: A. Remove the introduction.

feedback.text: Removing another required part weakens the format.

answer.text: B. Add a conclusion that restates the focus and closes the speech.

feedback.text: Correct. A conclusion is a required part that helps complete the speech format.

answer.text: C. Add unrelated details to make it longer.

feedback.text: Length does not fix a missing format part.

answer.text: D. Delete the support under each point.

feedback.text: Support is needed for a quality speech product.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U02_L04_GuidedPractice_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.PRES.02

Which question best checks speech product quality?

answer.text: A. Is it as long as possible?

feedback.text: Length does not prove quality.

answer.text: B. Does it include random details?

feedback.text: Random details weaken quality.

answer.text: C. Does each part help the speaker communicate clearly?

feedback.text: Correct. Quality depends on whether the format supports clear communication.

answer.text: D. Does it avoid all structure?

feedback.text: Avoiding structure works against format-specific quality.
